body.title: feat: setting to make the full list of members of an organization public
body.body:
This PR is split out from !15170, together with !15276, to make them smaller (hoping that reviewing it will be easier). If the combined PR is preferred, feel free to reopen and review that one instead.

This introduces a setting on organizations, to make their list of members fully public.

The existing membership visibility of users is still used to determine if the organization is shown on their personal profile. (A follow-up PR will move the visibility controls for their membership to their own list of organizations: https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/issues/7825).

This is for #862, following the design discussed in https://codeberg.org/forgejo/design/issues/64. The goal is to cater for the following use cases:
* keeping the existing visibility settings (which might not make a ton of sense, but as it's the current behavior, it's worth letting users preserve that if they're attached to it)
* the need for a completely transparent organization, where all members and teams are visible (which will be completed by the follow-up PR)
* the need to keep organizational structure partly hidden in certain cases, for instance for a company to have all members public but keep the internal corporate structure hidden, or hide the members of certain teams only.

The lists of members remain partial for logged-out users by default, as is currently the case. But for newly-created public organizations, the setting is enabled, so all members are shown.
For private organizations, the newly introduced setting is kept disabled, as one needs to be a member of the organization to be able to see its members list anyway.

body.title: feat: setting to make the list of teams of an organization public
body.body:
This PR is split out from !15170 to make it smaller (hoping that reviewing it will be easier).

This introduces a setting on an organization, to make its list of teams public.
That doesn't make the team members public. A follow-up PR will introduce a setting on each team, to determine if its members should be public too.

This is for #862, following the design discussed in https://codeberg.org/forgejo/design/issues/64. The goal is to cater for the following use cases:
* keeping the existing visibility settings (which might not make a ton of sense, but as it's the current behavior, it's worth letting users preserve that if they're attached to it)
* the need for a completely transparent organization, where all members and teams are visible (which will be completed by the follow-up PR)
* the need to keep organizational structure partly hidden in certain cases, for instance for a company to have all members public but keep the internal corporate structure hidden, or hide the members of certain teams only.

The lists of teams remain restricted to org members by default, as is currently the case. But for newly-created public organizations, the teams will be public by default.
For private organizations, the newly introduced setting is kept disabled, as one needs to be able to know of the existence of an organization to be able to see its teams.
